issues.display_title: Issue #1709: Return a Completion Flag for Each Portfolio Setup Step
issues.main_description_html:
• Endpoint: GET /portfolios/setup-steps — new route, separate from GET /portfolios

Context

The wizard needs to know which steps are complete to decide what is open and what is locked. Rather than having the frontend work that out for itself from a pile of raw fields, the API draws the conclusion and sends the result.

The rules then live in one place, and the frontend just reads them.

Its own endpoint, not bolted onto GET /portfolios. What needs it is the wizard sidebar, which appears on all four settings screens — not only the ones that happen to load portfolio detail.

Response shape

{
  "last_login": "...",
  "encrypt": "...",
  "setup_steps": {
    "about": true,
    "location": true,
    "featured": true,
    "template": false
  }
}
Step true when
about company_name, email, phone, logo_bg_color and title are all filled
location map_lat and map_lng are filled and non-zero
featured at least one of featured_listing_1, featured_listing_2, featured_listing_3 holds a tour
template about and location are both true

Acceptance criteria

  • GET /portfolios/setup-steps returns the four booleans for the logged-in user
  • Values follow the table above
  • featured is true only when at least one featured slot is filled; empty, null and 0 slots do not count
  • template follows about and location — it does not read xsl_template at all
  • An account that has never touched its portfolio returns all four booleans as false
  • GET /portfolios is unchanged

issues.display_title: Issue #1710: Exclude Already-Featured Businesses From the Add-Featured Search
issues.main_description_html:
• Endpoint: GET /portfolios/panoramas → listPortfolioPanoramas — the same tour list the portfolio page uses
  • Proposed new query param: exclude_featured=1

Context

The add-featured modal has no search endpoint of its own. It reuses the tour list (CreateFeaturedBusiness.jsx:24-45) with limit: 10, page: 1, search, type: 'name', and shows the result as the dropdown.

Duplicates are already rejected — but only after the customer has found and selected the business. Removing them from the list up front stops the dead end before it happens.

An optional flag on the existing endpoint is enough. No new route: the search, paging and filtering all already work there, and the param is off by default so the portfolio page is untouched.

Filtering on the frontend instead was considered and rejected — it would eat into the 10 results the dropdown asks for, so a customer with three featured businesses could see a short or empty list and think their search failed.

The featured entries live in the portfolio table as featured_listing_1..3 and hold the tour's Id — the same column the list query already selects (as id_portfolio), so the exclusion is a direct match.

Acceptance criteria

  • exclude_featured=1 removes already-featured businesses from the result
  • Holds even when the customer types the exact business name
  • The result still fills the requested limit where enough matches exist
  • Without the param the endpoint behaves exactly as it does today
